cs.t: I've got an old HP Z-620 workstation with dual E5-2697 v2 CPUs and 128GB of DDR3 RAM. The docs say it supports up to 192GB, but I wasn't able to get it to POST with all the RAM slots full. It's still a "homelab" beast and does great with development and GIS/Mapping applications. I was not able to figure out how to run AI workloads on it with decent performance, however, so I finally broke down and got a dedicated GPU for it. It's pretty great what can still be done with older hardware.
cs.th: A 10 year old Xeon is all you need (for 26B-A4B MTP Drafters without GPU)
